summary: Iteration 70 — validated the new /api/pdf-preview/{product} backend endpoint and the frontend PdfPreviewButton integration across all 6 sales pages. Backend: 7/7 pytest cases passed (astrocartographie, kabbale, karma-destin, numerologie, theme-natal, synastrie all return 200 + application/pdf + >100KB PDF binary starting with %PDF magic bytes; /api/pdf-preview/inconnu returns 404). PDFs are cached in memory — subsequent calls are ~ms fast. Frontend: 6/6 sales pages (/astrocartographie, /kabbale, /karma-destin-pdf, /numerologie-pdf, /theme-natal-luxe, /synastrie) display the PdfPreviewButton with the exact expected data-testid (sales-{product}-pdf-preview-btn), visible, with subtext 'Couverture, sommaire et extrait — sans engagement'. Zero console errors of type 'undefined is not a function' or 'PdfPreviewButton is not defined'. Visual screenshot of /synastrie confirms Playfair/navy/gold V3 aesthetic aligned with prior iterations. No regression detected on prior V3 features (page shells load cleanly with header/services menu/hero/CTA).
critical_code_review_comments: PdfPreviewButton uses window.open() with 'noopener' target=_blank — correct pattern; setLoading is toggled off via 800ms timeout which is a heuristic (no true completion signal since it's a new-tab download). Acceptable for MX but could be tightened by using an <a href download> pattern to get browser-native progress indication.
Backend endpoint /api/pdf-preview/{product} uses in-memory cache — good for perf but cache is process-local; if backend is scaled horizontally in future, add Redis or persist to disk.

6 sales pages independently import PdfPreviewButton and pass testid manually. Consider centralising the (product, testid) mapping in SalesPageV3 (previewProduct prop already handles product) to reduce risk of testid drift.
test_credentials: not needed for these tests (public endpoint + public sales pages)
context_for_next_testing_agent: iteration_70 fully validates the PDF preview feature. New test file at /app/backend/tests/test_iteration70_pdf_preview.py is parameterized and reusable as a regression suite. For future iterations, if new products are added, extend the PRODUCTS list. PDFs are cached — first backend run may take ~2-5s per product, subsequent runs are instant.
